Within the castle, the sept has rows of stained-glass windows honoring Garth Greenhand and the Seven. Highgarden's godswood houses three weirwoods known as the Three Singers. The palatial keep is adorned with statues and colonnades. Additionally, the castle features groves, fountains, and courtyards. The structures themselves are intertwined with ivy, grapevines, and climbing roses. Highgarden is a place of abundant flowers, filled with the melodies of singers, pipers, fiddlers, and harpers. The stables offer a splendid selection of horses. The fields surrounding the castle are adorned with golden roses that extend as far as the eye can see. Nearby orchards yield fruits such as melons, peaches, and fireplums.

entries.name: Arbor
entries.description: The Arbor is a golden island off the southwestern-most part of Westeros, ruled by House Redwyne. It is considered part of the Reach, and is separated from the mainland by the Redwyne Straits. It is protected by the Redwyne fleet, the largest fleet of the Seven Kingdoms. The Arbor is among the richest places of Westeros. The Arbor is known for making the best wine in Westeros, especially a terrific red one and a gold wine. Wine from the Arbor is usually sweeter than wine from Dorne. Peaches from the Arbor are huge and sweet. Traders from the Arbor have often sailed to Qarth. The Arbor has a warm and pleasant climate, due to its position surrounded by water off Westeros's southern coast.

entries.name: Fowler
entries.description: House Fowler of Skyreach is a noble house from Skyreach in Dorne. They hold the title of "Warden of the Prince's Pass" and watch over the Prince's Pass. The sigil of House Fowler is a hooded azure hawk on an argent (silver) field. The words of House Fowler are "Let Me Soar". House Fowler are vassals of House Yronwood. The current lord of House Fowler is Franklyn Fowler, called the Old Hawk. He is the father of the Fowler twins: Jennelyn Fowler and Jeyne Fowler, both are tall women with wispy yellow hair. In their youth twins played with Princess Arianne Martell in the pools of the Water Gardens.

entries.name: Allyrion
entries.description: House Allyrion of Godsgrace is a major Dornish noble house. Godsgrace sits near the confluence of the Scourge and the Vaith into the Greenblood. It is headed by Delonne Allyrion, the Lady of Godsgrace. Ser Ryon Allyrion is her son and heir. Ser Daemon Sand is Ryon's bastard son; Ryon has two more legitimate sons from Ynys Yronwood, his wife. Their blazon is a golden hand on gyronny red and black. Their words are "No Foe May Pass".

entries.name: Yronwood
entries.description: House Yronwood of Yronwood is the most powerful house in Dorne after the ruling Martells. Their seat, Yronwood, is the last fortress defending the Boneway; this is reflected in their title Warden of the Stone Way. Their words are "We Guard the Way". Their sigil is a black portcullis grill over sand. Yronwoods are stony dornishmen who tend to have blond hair and blue eyes. Lord Anders Yronwood is Lord of Yronwood, the Bloodroyal, and Warden of the Stone Way. Ynys Yronwood is Anders's eldest daughter, married to Ser Ryon Allyrion; she has at least two sons. Gwyneth Yronwood is Anders's youngest daughter. Ser Archibald Yronwood is Anders's cousin.

entries.name: Dayne
entries.description: House Dayne, a vassal of House Martell in Dorne, holds the castle of Starfall. Their ancestral weapon is Dawn, a blade forged from a fallen star. The wielder of Dawn is bestowed the title "the Sword of the Morning". Daynes are known for their hair, which can be pale blond, dark, or silver with a black streak, and their eyes, often dark blue or purple. House Dayne has a cadet branch, House Dayne of High Hermitage. Their sigil displays a white sword and falling star on a lilac field. Notably, House Dayne has two tragic figures: Ser Arthur Dayne, the Sword of the Morning, who perished at the Skirmish at the Tower of Joy, and Lady Ashara Dayne, who took her own life at Starfall. The current ruler, Edric Dayne, possesses fair, pale blond hair and dark blue eyes that resemble purple. He wears a pale purple cloak. While initially shy, Edric is known for his good-natured and polite demeanor.

entries.name: Martell
entries.description: House Martell of Sunspear is one of the Great Houses of Westeros and the ruling house of Dorne. They were never conquered by the Targaryens and have maintained a more isolated role in wider political events since Robert's Rebellion. House Martell's sigil is a red sun pierced by a golden spear, on an orange field. Their house words are "Unbowed, Unbent, Unbroken." The Martells have a reputation for being fierce and resilient, with a strong sense of independence. House Martell has been known for its skilled warriors and strategic military tactics, particularly their expertise in guerrilla warfare. Their vassals are: House Allyrion, House Blackmont, House Dalt, House Dayne, House Gargalen, House Jordayne, House Manwoody, House Qorgyle, House Santagar, House Uller, House Yronwood. House Martell is currently ruled by Prince Doran Martell, the head of House Martell, from Sunspear in southeastern Dorne. Princess Arianne Martell is Doran's daughter and the heir to Sunspear. Prince Quentyn Martell is Doran's brother. Prince Oberyn Martell is Doran's brother, known for his combat skills and fiery spirit. Ellaria Sand is Oberyn’s paramour and mother of his daughters. Areo Hotah is the Captain of the guards at Sunspear. Manfrey Martell, a knight of House Martell and a cousin to Doran Martell, is the castellan of Sunspear.

entries.name: Starfall
entries.description: Starfall is the ancestral castle of House Dayne in Dorne. The castle is located in the western Red Mountains on an island in the Torentine where it pours into the Summer Sea. Starfall includes a tower called the Palestone Sword.Northeast of Starfall is High Hermitage, the seat of a Dayne cadet branch.

entries.name: Water Gardens
entries.description: The Water Gardens is a palace with gardens and waterworks that serves as a private retreat to House Martell, the rulers of Dorne. The Gardens are located on a beach next to the Summer Sea, three leagues to the west of Sunspear on a coastal road. Pale pink marble paves the gardens and courtyard. Terraces overlooking the numerous pools and fountains of the Water Gardens, shaded by blood orange trees. The Water Gardens are pleasant in autumn: hot days, cool nights, the salt breeze blowing in from the sea, and fountains and pools to admire and play in. Children from all stations and areas of Dorne are sent to the Water Gardens to foster, where they play together at the beach, pools and fountains, and in the water.

entries.name: Planky Town
entries.description: The Planky Town is a trading town that lies at the mouth of the Greenblood in Dorne, near Lemonwood. The largest and most populous settlement in Dorne, the Planky Town has a harbor that sees trading vessels. The town is the chief harbor of Dorne. The Planky Town is a settlement that floats upon the river. The houses, halls, and shops are made of poleboats, barges, and merchant ships, lashed together with hempen rope and floating on the tide.

entries.name: Sunspear
entries.description: Sunspear, also known as the Old Palace, is where House Martell rules from and serves as the capital of Dorne. It's situated on the Broken Arm, which is north of the Greenblood along the far southeastern coast of Westeros. The castle is surrounded by the sea on three sides, with the shadow city on the fourth side. The Water Gardens, the palace, is located three leagues away on the coastal road. Doran Martell's captain of guards is Areo Hotah, and Caleotte and Myles serve as maesters for House Martell. Ricasso acts as the castle's seneschal, and Ser Manfrey Martell is the castellan. Alyse Ladybright holds the position of lord treasurer at Sunspear. Sunspear is a walled settlement, safeguarded by three massive Winding Walls that encircle each other. The Spear Tower, a tall and slender structure, stands at a height of one hundred and fifty feet and can house noble prisoners. The Tower of the Sun, a magnificent domed tower, contains the high seats of the Prince of Dorne. A portrait of Princess Daenerys Targaryen can be found hanging in Sunspear. The shadow city, adjacent to Sunspear, is a peculiar and dusty town built against one of Sunspear's walls, expanding westward. Further west, there are stables, inns, winesinks, and pillow houses, each with their own walls. Additional hovels have been constructed against these walls, resulting in a labyrinth of narrow alleys, homes, and bazaars.

entries.name: Brienne of Tarth
entries.description: Brienne of Tarth, also known as the Maid of Tarth, is a noblewoman from the island of Tarth in the Stormlands of Westeros. At the age of 20, she is the only surviving child of Lord Selwyn Tarth, who raised her alone after her mother's death during childbirth. From a young age, Brienne displayed a strong and independent nature that set her apart from the expectations placed on noblewomen. At an impressive height of 6 feet 3 inches, Brienne possesses a muscular and robust physique, a result of her rigorous combat training. Her features are strong and broad, with sandy blonde hair kept short for practicality. Her most captivating trait is her piercing blue eyes. Brienne is renowned for her unwavering loyalty, integrity, and dedication to honor. Despite the challenges she faces due to her gender and appearance, she remains resolute in her pursuit of proving herself in a world that underestimates her. Independence and adherence to her principles, rooted in chivalry and knighthood, define her character. Having devoted her life to the art of combat, Brienne has become a remarkable warrior, defying societal expectations. Her prowess in swordplay, combined with her strength, agility, and determination, make her a formidable opponent on the battlefield. Additionally, her proficiency in horsemanship, gained through extensive training on Tarth, further enhances her skills. Brienne's dreams of becoming a knight. She idolizes the heroic knights of Westeros and avidly reads historical texts and tales that depict their valor. Her quest for honor and justice fuels her determination to always choose the right path, even in the face of adversity. Brienne's relationship with her father, Lord Selwyn Tarth, is complex. While he loves his daughter, he struggles to comprehend her aspirations of becoming a knight. Nevertheless, Brienne's unwavering resolve has earned her his reluctant respect. As a child, she was frequently ridiculed by her peers when dressed in female clothes, but she was once rescued from such mockery by a young Renly Baratheonю She has formed a close bond with Renly Baratheon, the younger brother of King Robert Baratheon, who recognizes her exceptional skill and appoints her to his personal guard.

entries.name: Tarth
entries.description: House Tarth of Evenfall Hall is a noble house from Evenfall Hall in the Stormlands. The family rules Tarth, a beautiful island northeast of Shipbreaker Bay that controls the Straits of Tarth between the island and mainland Westeros. They are one of the main houses sworn to House Baratheon of Storm's End. Their sigil is quartered with yellow suns on rose and white crescent moons on azure. Lord Selwyn Tarth is the head of the house, and his heir is Brienne Tarth, a formidable warrior. His lady wife died not long after the birth of Brienne.

entries.name: Howland Reed
entries.description: Lord Howland Reed is the head of House Reed of Greywater Watch. He is a crannogman, a member of a distinct group of people living in the swamps and marshes of the Neck in the North of Westeros. Crannogmen are known to be shorter and smaller than most men in Westeros. He is a loyal vassal of House Stark, ruling over the bog-filled lands of the Neck and the crannogmen. He first met the members of House Stark, including Brandon, Eddard, and Benjen, at the great tourney at Harrenhal when he was a young man. During the tourney, Howland was tormented by three squires until Lyanna Stark came to his defense. Howland fought alongside Eddard Stark during Robert's Rebellion and participated in the Skirmish at the Tower of Joy. He saved Eddard Stark's life during the battle by stabbing Ser Arthur Dayne from behind. Howland is known for his knowledge of the terrain and guerrilla tactics, which he uses to defend the North from invaders. He is skilled in combat. Howland is the father of Meera and Jojen Reed.

entries.name: the Twins
entries.description: The Twins, also called the Crossing, is the home of House Frey in the northern riverlands. It's south of the bogs of the Neck and west of the kingsroad. The Twins is a strong fortress that consists of two identical castles, connected by a tower in the middle of the bridge. The castles are made of stone and stand on the banks of the Green Fork, where the river flows swiftly and deeply. Brenett is the maester of the castles, and Lame Lothar, one of Lord Walder Frey's sons, serves as the steward. Jinglebell, Walder's grandson, entertains as a fool, and Sedgekins works as a servant. They have high walls, deep moats, and a barbican and portcullis in each. Moats surround the castles, turning them into islands. The Lord of the Crossing sits in a great hall in the east castle on a tall and massive chair made of black oak. The back of the chair is carved to resemble two towers connected by an arched bridge. The maester's chambers are located in a turret accessible from Lord Frey's hall via a covered bridge. There's an apple orchard and a cornfield near the eastern castle, while hills can be found to the west.

entries.name: Tyrell
entries.description: House Tyrell of Highgarden is one of the Great Houses of the Seven Kingdoms. They are the rulers of the Reach. They are a wealthy and influential house, second only to House Lannister in terms of riches among the Great Houses. The Tyrells have the largest armies and, when combined with the Redwyne fleet, the lords of the Shield Islands, and the coastal lords, they possess a navy that rivals or even surpasses the royal fleet of King's Landing. Their sigil is a golden rose on a green background, and their motto is "Growing Strong." Members of the family typically have curly brown hair and brown eyes. The vassals of House Tyrell include House Ashford, House Caswell, House Florent, House Fossoway, House Hastwyck, House Hightower, House Leygood, House Merryweather, House Mullendore, House Redwyne, House Rowan, and House Tarly. Lord Mace Tyrell is the current head of House Tyrell, ruling from Highgarden. His son and heir, Willas Tyrell, is known for his intelligence and love for books, he has a crippled leg. Garlan Tyrell, Mace's second son, is a skilled and honorable knight, often referred to as Garlan the Gallant; he is married to Leonette Fossoway and holds the title of Lord of Brightwater Keep. Margaery Tyrell, Mace's daughter, is a beautiful and ambitious woman skilled in courtly intrigue. Loras Tyrell, Mace's third son, is known as the "Knight of Flowers" and is highly skilled in jousting and warfare. Lady Olenna Tyrell, also known as Lady Olenna or the "Queen of Thorns," is the sharp-witted matriarch of the family and Mace's mother. Lady Mina Tyrell, Mace's sister, is married to Lord Paxter Redwyne. Lady Janna Tyrell, another sister of Mace, is married to Ser Jon Fossoway.

entries.name: Bolton
entries.description: House Bolton of the Dreadfort is a Great House in Westeros. The Boltons are notorious for their brutal tradition of flaying enemies alive, which was depicted on their sigil—a flayed man. Their sigil is an inverted red flayed man with white, cross-shaped flayed skin behind him, set against a black background. Their motto is "Our Blades Are Sharp," while a commonly uttered phrase among their members is "A naked man has few secrets; a flayed man, none." House Bolton is sworn to House Stark, but they act in their own interests. There's a long history of tension between House Bolton and House Stark. House Bolton had several vassal houses: House Burley, House Harclay, House Knott, House Liddle, House Norrey, and House Wull. They also have vassals on Skagos, including House Crowl of Deepdown, House Magnar of Kingshouse, and House Stane of Driftwood Hall. Roose Bolton is the head of the house. Lady Walda is his current wife of House Frey. Ramsay Bolton is Roose's legitimized bastard son by a miller's wife.

entries.name: Dreadfort
entries.description: The Dreadfort is a fortress in the north and the seat of House Bolton in northeastern Westeros. Located on the banks of the upper Weeping Water, it is southeast of the Lonely Hills and north of the Sheepshead Hills. The Dreadfort is north of Hornwood, south of Last Hearth, and southwest of Karhold. Steelshanks Walton serves as Lord Roose Bolton's captain and Nage is one of his guards. Ben Bones is the castle's kennelmaster and Tybald serves as maester. Letters from the Dreadfort use pink sealing wax. The Dreadfort is a strong fortress, with high walls and triangular merlons that look like sharp stone teeth. Its great hall is dim and smoky, with rows of torches grasped by skeletal human hands jutting from the walls. Long tables stand before a dais with a high table. The hall has a vaulted ceiling and wooden rafters turned black from smoke. The Dreadfort is ill omened, for it is said the Boltons keep torture chambers and a special room where they hang the flayed skins of their enemies, including several Kings in the North. Boltons are buried beneath the Dreadfort.

entries.name: Karstark
entries.description: House Karstark of Karhold is a noble house from Karhold in the north. They were founded as a cadet branch of their overlords, the Starks of Winterfell, and were among their principal bannermen. The sigil of House Karstark is a white sunburst on black. Their words are "The Sun of Winter". The head of the house is Lord Rickard Karstark. He has four children: Harrion, Eddard, Torrhen, and Alys.

entries.name: Gates of the Moon
entries.description: The Gates of the Moon, also known as the Gates, is a castle at the base of the Giant's Lance in the Vale of Arryn. It is held by Lord Nestor Royce, High Steward of the Vale and Keeper of the Gates of the Moon, on behalf of House Arryn. Larger than the Eyrie, the Gates of the Moon is a stout castle with a moat, a gatehouse, a yard, and a well. The castle has square towers, include the East Tower and the Falcon Tower. The back of the castle's Great Hall has a pillared gallery which leads to tower stairs and to the inner ward. The castle's vaults contain granaries and dungeons. Prisoners can also be kept in tower cells. Guardsmen at the Gates of the Moon wear sky-blue cloaks. At night torches flicker at the castle's ramparts and the moon is reflected in its moat. Beyond the upper bailey's postern gate is a dense forest of pine and spruce, as well as the steep, carved steps along the Giant's Lance.[2] Mules are kept at the Gates of the Moon to help transport travelers up the mountain to Stone, Snow, and Sky.[2]

entries.name: White Harbor
entries.description: White Harbor is a harbor city up north with the New Castle, the home of House Manderly. It's southeast of Winterfell and the biggest settlement in the north, though the smallest among the five major cities in Westeros. White Harbor is the main trading port in the north, thanks to its position at the mouth of the White Knife River, which allows for trade further north. Because of its location, White Harbor has more contact with the south of Westeros and has a diverse population. It's a clean and well-organized city, with wide straight streets made of cobblestone that are great for walking. The houses are made of whitewashed stone, and the roofs are steep and dark grey. The city is protected by city guards. White Harbor has access to a variety of seafood, and it's also known for its shipwrights and silversmiths. The city is famous for its beer. Ships often sail between White Harbor and the Three Sisters, trading wood, wool, and hides for crab, fish, and goat cheese. Fishfoot Yard is a square with a fountain in the middle, just outside the Seal Gate. There's an alley that leads to a brothel. The Lazy Eel is a tavern known for its old prostitutes, terrible wine, and inedible meat pies. The Sept of the Snows is a large sept with a domed roof and tall statues of the Seven. The New Castle is where House Manderly resides. It sits on a hill inside the city walls, and you can reach its gates from the Wolf's Den below by using the Castle Stair. There's a secret passage underneath the Castle Stair that connects the New Castle with the cellars of the Wolf's Den.

entries.name: Addam Marbrand
entries.description: Ser Addam Marbrand, a member of House Marbrand, is the son and heir of Lord Damon Marbrand of Ashemark. He is a trusted ally of House Lannister, acting as their bannerman. He has a lean and athletic build, with dark copper hair that falls to his shoulders. He is very brave, gallant and charming. He is highly skilled in horsemanship and swordfighting. Addam is a childhood friend of Jaime Lannister. He attends council meetings with Tywin, providing his insights.

entries.name: Blackmont
entries.description: House Blackmont of Blackmont is a major Dornish noble house. Their seat, Blackmont, is on the banks of the Torentine in the Red Mountains of Dorne. House Blackmont has very little Rhoynar ancestry compared to other Dornish houses, as they primarily descend from the First Men and Andals. This makes them light-haired and light-skinned. House Blackmont's sigil is a black vulture with a pink infant in its claws on a yellow field. Lady Larra Blackmont is the Lady of Blackmont and the head of the house. Jynessa Blackmont is her daughter and heir to Blackmont. Perros Blackmont is her son, a squire. Lady Larra has a few younger children who are among the favorite children hosted by Doran Martell, Prince of Dorne, at the Water Gardens.

entries.name: Gargalen
entries.description: House Gargalen of Salt Shore is a major Dornish noble house. Their seat, Salt Shore, is located along the Summer Sea on the southern coast of Dorne. Deceased Doran Martell, the former Prince of Dorne, squired for Lord Gargalen in his youth. The sigil of House Gargalen is a red cockatrice with a black snake in its beak on a golden field. Lord Tremond Gargalen, the Lord of Salt Shore, is the head of the house.

entries.name: Jordayne
entries.description: House Jordayne of the Tor is one of the principal noble houses of Dorne. The Tor is situated on the southern coast of the Sea of Dorne. Their sigil is a golden quill on checkered dark and light green. Their words are "Let it be Written". Lord Trebor Jordayne is the Lord of the Tor and the head of the house. Myria Jordayne is his daughter and heir to the Tor.

entries.name: Manwoody
entries.description: House Manwoody of Kingsgrave is an old Dornish noble house. Its seat, Kingsgrave, is placed amidst the Prince's Pass, guarding access to Dorne. The sigil of House Manwoody is a crowned skull on a black field. Their words are "No King Above Me". Lord Dagos Manwoody is the Lord of Kingsgrave and the head of the house. Mors Manwoody is his eldest son and heir. Dickon Manwoody is his second son. Ser Myles Manwoody is Dagos's brother.

entries.name: Qorgyle
entries.description: House Qorgyle of Sandstone is a noble house from Sandstone, located in the dunes of western Dorne. They are among the principal bannermen sworn to House Martell of Sunspear. Members of House Qorgyle are known as Sandy Dornishmen, characterized by their dark olive skin and black hair. The sigil of House Qorgyle consists of three black scorpions on a crimson field. The words of House Qorgyle are "Fear Our Sting". Their home is an oasis amidst the sands. The house consists of Lord Quentyn Qorgyle, Lord of Sandstone; Ser Gulian Qorgyle, his eldest son and heir to Sandstone; Ser Arron Qorgyle, his second son.

entries.name: Santagar
entries.description: House Santagar of Spottswood is a house of landed knights from Spottswood in Dorne. They are sworn to House Martell. The Santagars are known for their martial prowess. The sigil of House Santagar is a spotted leopard with a golden axe on a blue and white field. The words of House Santagar are "Woe to Who Touches It". Ser Symon Santagar is the Knight of Spottswood and the current head of the house. Sylva Santagar, called "Spotted Sylva", is his daughter and heir to Spottswood. Sylva has many freckles. Sylva is married to Lord Eldon Estermont of Estermont.

entries.name: Uller
entries.description: House Uller of Hellholt is one of the great noble houses in Dorne. Their keep, the Hellholt, is in the middle of the Dornish desert, and they are reputed to be impulsive and unpredictable. A Dornish saying is "Half of the Ullers are half-mad, and the other half are worse." Their arms are rayonne yellow over crimson. Lord Harmen Uller is Lord of Hellholt and the current head of the house. Ellaria Sand, his bastard daughter is a paramour to Prince Oberyn Martell and mother of four of his bastard daughters. Ser Ulwyck Uller is Harmen's brother.

entries.name: Dragonstone
entries.description: Dragonstone is a castle on the island of the same name at the entrance to Blackwater Bay, below the Dragonmont. It was the original seat of House Targaryen in Westeros, and now Dragonstone is owned by Lord Stannis Baratheon, the younger brother of King Robert Baratheon. Shaped from stone to look like dragons, the castle has a dark reputation. The maesters at Dragonstone are Cressen and Pylos, and the castle's sept is maintained by Septon Barre. At least two members of House Blackberry serve at Dragonstone. Dragonstone was constructed by the Valyrians using mystical arts, fire, and sorcery. Throughout the castle, dragon motifs can be found, like small dragon sculptures adorning gates and dragon claws gripping torches. The armory and smithy are covered by a pair of grand wings, while dragon tails form archways and staircases. The citadel itself is crafted entirely from black stone. Dragonstone encompasses a castle yard and a library. Beneath the curtain walls lies a fishing village with a port. It has the Stone Drum, a colossal tower and central keep. To reach the Stone Drum from Sea Dragon Tower, one must cross the gallery and pass through the middle and inner walls. A high stone bridge, spanning emptiness, leads from the Stone Drum to the entrance of the dungeons. The top floor of the Stone Drum houses the Chamber of the Painted Table, where a large table intricately carved and painted as a map of Westeros can be found. The Great Hall, shaped like a massive dragon lying on its belly, features heavy red doors set within its mouth. The kitchens resemble a curled-up dragon, with smoke and heat venting through its nostrils. Sea Dragon Tower, resembling a dragon gazing calmly at the sea, contains the maester's chambers and the rookery. The Windwyrm is a tower shaped like a defiant screaming dragon. Aegon's Garden, accessed by descending past the arch of the Dragon's Tail, houses tall dark trees, wild roses, towering thorny hedges, and cranberries. The garden exudes a pleasant piney fragrance. The sept of Dragonstone, dedicated to the Faith of the Seven, houses statues carved from the masts of the ships that carried the first Targaryens from Valyria. Beneath Dragonstone, a turnpike stair and smooth stony passages lead to cells. The walls in the dark dungeon emit warmth when touched.

entries.name: Jon Arryn
entries.description: Jon Arryn is the Lord of the Eyrie, the Defender of the Vale, the Warden of the East and the head of House Arryn. Jon Arryn rebelled against the Mad King Aerys II Targaryen after he condoned the alleged kidnapping of Eddard Stark's sister, Lyanna, who was also betrothed to Robert Baratheon. After the rebel victory, Robert Baratheon became king and appointed Jon Arryn as his Hand. Jon Arryn married Lady Jeyne Royce as his first wife, but their daughter was stillborn. His second wife, Lady Rowena, died without issue. Jon Arryn's third and current wife was Lysa Tully is much younger than him. Their marriage was part of an alliance between House Arryn and House Tully. Jon and Lysa have a son, Robert. Jon acted as a second father to Lord Eddard Stark and King Robert when they were children. Jon has broad shoulders. Half of his teeth had fallen out by the time he married Lysa Tully. He has blue eyes, blond hair, and an aquiline nose. Lysa resents Jon's poor breath. Jon has a reputation for being prudent, calming and wise, and kindly and trusting. He is cordial but not friendly toward Lord Stannis Baratheon. Jon's blade has wings on its crossguard, a falcon-head pommel, and is engraved in silver to resemble mountain sky. Jon preferrs functional armor, rather than jeweled and silvered plate. Jon's favorite bird is a falcon gifted to him by Robert. Jon Arryn is around 60 years old.

entries.name: Robb Stark
entries.description: Robb Stark is the eldest son of Eddard Stark and Catelyn Tully and is the heir of House Stark to Winterfell and the north. He is called the Young Wolf by friend and foe alike. He is 14. Robb has a stocky build, blue eyes, and thick red-brown hair. He is strong and fast. He wields a longsword and an oak shield decorated with a direwolf's head. Robb is better with a lance than his half brother, Jon Snow, although Jon is more skilled with a sword. Robb is his father Eddard's son, with a keen sense of justice and courtesy. He shares his father's devotion to honor and is frequently accompanied by his direwolf, Grey Wind. He has a strong bond with his family, particularly with his father, whom he admires and looks up to. Robb shares a loving and caring relationship with his mother, Catelyn Stark. He respects her opinions and values her guidance. Robb's relationship with his sister Sansa is mostly positive. They have a typical sibling dynamic, with occasional disagreements and arguments. Robb is protective of Sansa and wants to ensure her well-being. Robb appreciates Arya's independent spirit and her determination to be her own person. Robb Stark and Jon Snow share a close and special bond. They spend a lot of time together, training in swordsmanship and learning the ways of the North. They share common interests and often confide in each other.

entries.name: Catelyn Stark
entries.description: Catelyn Stark, also called Lady Stark, comes from House Tully, a notable family in Westeros. She was born and raised in Riverrun, the ancestral home of House Tully in the fertile Riverlands. Catelyn, the eldest daughter of Lord Hoster Tully, grew up with her younger siblings, Lysa and Edmure. At 16, Catelyn entered into an arranged marriage with Eddard Stark, the Lord of Winterfell and Warden of the North. Originally, Catelyn was supposed to marry Eddard's brother, Brandon Stark, but he died and she wed Ned instead. Together, Catelyn and Eddard have five children: Robb, Sansa, Arya, Bran, and Rickon. Catelyn deeply loves and cares for her children but dislikes Eddard's illegitimate son, Jon Snow, who lives with them in Winterfell. Catelyn Stark has a graceful and regal presence, with auburn hair and blue eyes, signature of the Tully family. She carries herself with poise, embodying authority and resilience. Known for her unwavering loyalty and strong sense of duty, Catelyn always puts her family's well-being first. She is a devoted wife and mother, prioritizing the needs of her loved ones over her own. Catelyn is intelligent and skilled in diplomacy, having a keen ability to judge character. She has some political influence through her childhood friend, Petyr Baelish, who is the king's master of coin and advisor in King's Landing. Catelyn actively participates in her children's education, teaching them the values of honor, loyalty, and duty. She shares a deep bond with her husband, Eddard Stark, based on trust, respect, and support. Catelyn is his closest confidante and advisor, offering counsel on political matters. She also maintains strong relationships with her siblings, especially Lysa. Catelyn values her family connections and works to protect and strengthen them.

entries.name: Eddard Stark
entries.description: Eddard Stark, also known as "Ned," leads House Stark, rules Winterfell, and protects the North. He's a close friend of King Robert I Baratheon, they grew up together. Ned has a long face, dark grey eyes, brown hair, and a greying beard that makes him seem older than his thirty-five years. Eddard Stark is known for his strong sense of honor, duty, and loyalty. He is a man of integrity and principles, always striving to do what is right. Eddard is a devoted husband and father, and he values family above all else. He is respected by his bannermen and the people of the North for his fairness and just rule. Eddard is also known for his wisdom and ability to make sound judgments. He is a capable leader and administrator, effectively managing the affairs of House Stark and the North. He wields a sword and a dagger and has a Valyrian steel greatsword, Ice. Ned is proficient in combat. Ned was born at Winterfell as the second son of Lord Rickard Stark and Lady Lyarra Stark. He had an older brother named Brandon and two younger siblings, Lyanna and Benjen. From age eight, Ned lived with Lord Jon Arryn at the Eyrie and formed a strong bond with his ward, Robert Baratheon. Jon Arryn became a father figure to him. Lyanna Stark, Eddard's younger sister, was betrothed to Robert Baratheon but was allegedly kidnapped by Prince Rhaegar Targaryen, leading to Robert's Rebellion. Lyanna died during it and her death had a profound impact on Eddard. Eddard's father and brother were executed by King Aerys II Targaryen, the Mad King, which led to Eddard becoming the Lord of Winterfell and Warden of the North. Ned married Catelyn Tully and they have five children: Robb, Sansa, Arya, Bran, and Rickon. Ned also brought Jon Snow to Winterfell. Catelyn and Eddard shares a strong bond, they have a loving and supportive marriage. Ned is cautious of Roose Bolton.

entries.name: Robert Baratheon
entries.description: Robert I Baratheon is the King and leader of House Baratheon in King's Landing. He is 35. He has two younger brothers, Stannis and Renly. He won the throne through conquest in the war known as Robert's Rebellion, which started when Rhaegar Targaryen, the Prince of Dragonstone, allegedly abducted Robert's betrothed, Lyanna Stark. Robert's victory at the Battle of the Trident, where he killed Rhaegar in a duel, turned the tide of the war in his favor. After the war, he married Cersei Lannister to solidify an alliance with House Lannister, but their marriage lacked love and respect. Robert and Cersei have three children: Joffrey, Myrcella, and Tommen. Robert has the typical Baratheon appearance, with black hair and bright blue eyes. He is a tall man, around six and a half feet tall. In his youth, Robert was handsome and clean-shaven, with rough hands. However, he gained a considerable amount of weight after Greyjoy's Rebellion due to excessive eating and drinking. His beard is thick and wild, hiding his double chin. Soldiers admire Robert for his bravery, but he can be headstrong, impulsive, and impatient. He is proud and stubborn, especially when under the influence of alcohol. As king, he is not accustomed to being challenged and can be easily manipulated by others. Tyrion Lannister sees him as a boastful fool, while Varys views him as a simple-minded individual. Cersei considers him ignorant, slow-witted, and lacking the ruthlessness she believes a king should possess. Petyr Baelish believes Robert deliberately turns a blind eye to unpleasant truths. In battle, Robert is as strong as a bull and fearless. He enjoys the clash of swords and despises poison as a cowardly weapon. He can show mercy to defeated enemies who display honesty and bravery, and he can inspire loyalty and friendship in those he spares. He holds a deep hatred for the Targaryens. Despite his physical decline, Robert remains a formidable man. Robert is notorious for his insatiable appetites and numerous affairs, resulting in many illegitimate children. However, he also possesses a reckless generosity. Robert's greatest strength lies in his ability to forge alliances and his charismatic leadership. Stannis recalls that men who fought against Robert during the day would often be drinking, feasting, and laughing with him in the evening. He has a good sense of humor and takes slights well openly on most occasions unless they are towards people he loves.

entries.name: Kevan Lannister
entries.description: Kevan Lannister is a knight from House Lannister, the younger brother of Tywin Lannister, the older brother of Genna Lannister. He was born as the second son of Lord Tytos Lannister. Kevan is a big man with broad shoulders and a thick waist. His short blond hair is balding, and he has a close-cropped, yellow beard that follows the line of his massive jaw. Kevan has green eyes and fair skin. Kevan is devoted to his elder brother, Lord Tywin. He is tireless, prudent, and reliable, solid and steady. Despite being a household knight and not a lord, Kevan's strategic thinking, significant retinue, and personal wealth has made him a man of significant standing. Kevan was a confidant and companion for Tywin since childhood. Recognizing the competency of Tywin at an early age, Kevan did his best to realize his brother's wishes, though this meant perpetually living in his shadow. In contrast to Kevan, Tywin had stormy relations with his other brothers, Tygett and Gerion. At sixteen, Tywin had Kevan collect the outstanding debts owed to Casterly Rock, and those who could not pay immediately had to surrender a family member as a hostage till the debt was settled. As Ser Harys Swyft was not able to pay at the time, he handed his daughter Dorna into Kevan's custody. Kevan fell in love with Dorna and married her by 266 AC. Ser Kevan had four children with his wife: Lancel, twin boys Martyn and Willem, and a daughter, Janei. Kevan considers his wife a gentle soul, never comfortable except at home with friends and kin around her.

entries.name: Storm's End
entries.description: Storm's End is the stronghold of House Baratheon, the ruling family of the Stormlands. It sits on Durran's Point, along the northern coast of Shipbreaker Bay. The castle is south of Bronzegate and northeast of Griffin's Roost. The kingsroad runs north from Storm's End through the stormlands to King's Landing, the capital of the Seven Kingdoms. Renly Baratheon is the Lord of Storm's End, aided by Maester Jurne. The castle is surrounded by a massive outer curtain wall, reaching heights of one hundred feet and thicknesses of forty to eighty feet. The wall is made of pale grey stone with a sturdy core of sand and rubble. It has a smooth, curved design that prevents the wind from having any impact. On the seaward side, there's a sheer drop of one hundred fifty feet into the sea. Behind the curtain wall, you'll find the castle's kitchens, stables, and yard. Storm's End features a single tower, a colossal drum tower with imposing battlements. The main hall of the castle is called the Round Hall. At the top of the tower, one'll find the maester's cell and the rookery. In the godswood of Storm's End, there's a weirwood tree with a solemn face carved into its trunk.

entries.name: Theon Greyjoy
entries.description: Theon Greyjoy, a member of House Greyjoy, is the only surviving son and future heir of Balon Greyjoy, the ruler of the Iron Islands. He has an older sister, Yara. Following the end of Greyjoy's Rebellion, Theon was taken as a hostage and placed under the care of Lord Eddard Stark in Winterfell. He is currently 14 years old. Theon is a slim and attractive young man with dark hair and a dark complexion. He finds amusement in almost everything and is known for his self-assured demeanor and smug smile. Despite his outward confidence, Theon hides insecurities relating to his uncertain familial and social identity. Theon seeks approval from the Starks, but usually feels unsatisfied. Skilled in hunting and horseback riding, Theon excels with the longbow and wields a dirk. He carries a longsword in a scabbard displaying the Greyjoy colors of black and gold. Theon considers himself a graceful dancer.

entries.name: Baratheon
entries.description: House Baratheon of Storm's End is one of the Great Houses of Westeros, and is the principal house in the stormlands, which they rule as Lords Paramount of the Stormlands. Their seat, Storm's End, is an ancient castle raised by the Storm Kings from the now-extinct House Durrandon. The Baratheon sigil is a crowned black stag on a field of gold. Their words are "Ours is the Fury". After Robert's Rebellion, House Baratheon split into three branches: Lord Robert Baratheon was crowned king and took residence at King's Landing, thereby creating House Baratheon of King's Landing. Robert gave the seat of Dragonstone to his younger brother, Stannis, creating House Baratheon of Dragonstone. Robert's youngest brother, Renly, became the Lord of Storm's End, continuing House Baratheon of Storm's End. Members of the family tend to be tall and powerfully built, with black hair and blue eyes, as well as strong, square jawlines. They are known for their mercurial tempers. Vassals: House Caron, House Connington, House Dondarrion, House Errol, House Estermont, House Fell, House Grandison, House Lonmouth, House Morrigen, House Musgood, House Peasebury, House Penros, House Seaworth, House Selmy, House Swann, House Tarth, House Trant, House Wylde. Robert Baratheon: The head of House Baratheon, King of the Seven Kingdoms, married to Cersei Lannister. Queen Cersei Baratheon (formerly Lannister) - Robert's wife and queen consort. Prince Joffrey Baratheon - Robert and Cersei's eldest son and heir to the Iron Throne. Prince Tommen Baratheon - Robert and Cersei's younger son. Princess Myrcella Baratheon - Robert and Cersei's daughter.

entries.name: Jaime Lannister
entries.description: Jaime is a member of House Lannister, the son of Tywin and Joanna Lannister. He is 34, exceptionally handsome, with golden hair and green eyes. He is known for his physical attractiveness and charm, which often captivates those around him. He has a twin sister, Cersei Lannister and a younger brother, Tyrion Lannister. Due to his position in the Kingsguard, Jaime cannot inherit his father's lands or titles. Jaime is arrogant and self-assured, often displaying a cocky and confident demeanor. He is known for his wit and sharp tongue, often engaging in clever banter and wordplay. Jaime doesn't mock others over minor insults the way Cersei does, and he can muster up polite behavior, but he is usually very blunt and straightforward. Jaime became extremely disillusioned with ideals of honor and loyalty when he saw firsthand the atrocities committed by the Mad King, how other "honorable" members of the Kingsguard stood by and did nothing while King Aerys had people burned alive for imagined insults. Jaime's reputation is tarnished by his infamous act of killing King Aerys II Targaryen, earning him the derogatory nickname "Kingslayer." Jaime was never politically ambitious, much to Cersei's annoyance, and often turns down her frequent urgings that he should try to become Hand of the King. Jaime is regarded as one of the best swordsmen in the Seven Kingdoms, known for his exceptional fighting skills and prowess with a sword. He is a skilled knight and a member of the Kingsguard, an elite group of knights sworn to protect the king. Jaime's combat abilities and martial skills are highly respected and feared by his adversaries. Jaime has a secret incestuous relationship with his twin sister, Cersei, which resulted in the birth of their three children: Joffrey, Myrcella, and Tommen. Jaime's relationship with his younger brother Tyrion is characterized by genuine affection and support. Jaime is the only member of Tyrion's immediate family who ever treated him with respect or kindness. In fact, he admires Tyrion's intellect and his ability to tell off those who insult him. Jaime never approved of Tywin and Cersei's long history of abuse towards Tyrion, and has always treated him like a brother. Jaime is the only member of the core Lannister family who has a reasonably good relationship with all of the others.

entries.name: Cersei Lannister
entries.description: Cersei Lannister is the queen of the Seven Kingdoms, she's 34. She is the daughter of Lord Tywin Lannister and Joanna Lannister, and the older twin of Jaime Lannister, older sister to Tyrion Lannister. She grew up in Casterly Rock. From a young age, she was prepared for a life of power and influence. When Cersei was four, her mother died in childbirth, and she held a grudge against Tyrion, blaming him for her death. Cersei had hopes of marrying Rhaegar Targaryen, but that dream never came true. At 19, she wed King Robert Baratheon in a political alliance, becoming the Queen. Initially, Cersei was infatuated with Robert's handsome appearance. However, their love quickly faded as Robert continued to pine for his deceased love, Lyanna Stark, and even called Cersei by Lyanna's name on their wedding night. She bore a son with Robert, who tragically died shortly after birth. Cersei grew to resent Robert for his infidelity and his lack of affection towards her. She felt trapped in a loveless marriage and turned to Jaime for emotional and physical comfort, maintaining an incestuous relationship with him. Her three children, Joffrey, Myrcella, and Tommen, are officially recognized as Robert's heirs, but in reality, they are the offspring of Cersei and Jaime's secret relationship. Cersei Lannister is famous for her stunning appearance, with long, golden curls, a porcelain-like face, and green eyes. She exudes confidence and elegance, always adorned in lavish attire and jewelry. Ambitious, cunning, and merciless, Cersei will stop at nothing to protect and secure her family's power and position, often resorting to manipulation and betrayal. With a strong sense of entitlement, Cersei firmly believes in her destined greatness. Her love for her children knows no bounds, and she is willing to do whatever it takes to shield them from harm. Her talent for manipulation allows her to exploit others for her own gain. Cersei's relationship with her father Tywin Lannister is complex. She wants his approval and respect but often clashes with his expectations.

entries.name: Dragonlord
entries.description: Dragonlords are the dragon-riding most powerful nobles of the Valyrian Freehold. Leadership of the Valyrian Freehold was contested by twoscore noble families who normally gathered in Valyria. Strong in sorcery, the dragonlords use binding spells and horns to control their dragons, and they used dragonflame to reshape stone into decorative shapes. Dragonlords considered themselves more powerful than gods. The dragonlords are inhumanly beautiful. Heraldic banners were not used by dragonlords.

entries.name: Valyrian peninsula
entries.description: The Valyrian peninsula is a large peninsula extending south from Essos into the Summer Sea. It is the heartland of the Valyrian Freehold and the location of the city of Valyria, capital of the Valyrian Freehold. The Fourteen Flames extend across the neck of the peninsula.

entries.name: Valyria
entries.description: The City of Valyria is a sprawling metropolis of grandeur, it is a cityscape that seems to defy imagination. Towering spires, forged from dragon-forged stone and enchanted metals, reach towards the skies, adorned with intricate carvings depicting the majesty of dragons in flight. Canals of molten silver and gold weave through the city. Marketplaces bustle with activity, filled with merchants peddling exotic wares that the Valyrians alone can master. The air is thick with the scent of arcane incense. In the heart of Valyria lies the Dragonspire, a colossal citadel that serves as both a seat of governance and a center of magical learning. The Dragonspire's towers pierce the sky, and within its hallowed halls, scholars and sorcerers delve into the mysteries of magic, while dragons roost on terraces overlooking the city. In the Towering spires and citadels dwell the great and most powerful Valyrian noble families. Valyria is on the Valyrian peninsula. Valyria is connected by dragon roads with other cities of the Freehold. Valyria is composed of four main districts: The Civic Centre, the oldest district, served as the city's seat of power. The Industrial Area, situated at the foot of the mountain. It was home to slave quarters, aqueducts, and bathhouses. The Port served as the residential quarter, home to the Valyrian navy as well as teeming street markets. The Forum, the center of social and public life in Valyria. Designed to impress visitors, its buildings were much grander than the rest of the city. At its end, parallel to the palace in the Civic Centre, sat the Bōjurlion, a massive arena.

entries.name: Fourteen Flames
entries.description: The Fourteen Flames is an immense chain of volcanoes extending across the Valyrian peninsula. There are deep mines beneath the Fourteen Flames. Valyria sent slaves to the mines beneath the Fourteen Flames, searching for gold, silver, and other ores. The worst slaves were sent down to die in the red darkness of the mines. The mines of Valyria are always hot and they grew hotter as shafts were driven deeper into the earth. The slaves toiled in an oven, the rocks around them too hot to touch. The air stank of brimstone and seared the slaves' lungs as they breathed. Certain shafts were cut so low that slaves had to crawl or bend. Slaves perished by the score, but the Valyrians did not care.

entries.name: Tyria
entries.description: Tyria is a city in Essos. It lies across the Smoking Sea from Oros and is connected by Valyrian road to the city of Valyria, which lies to the south of the island. Tyria was founded by the Valyrian Freehold. Although rich and glorious, it did not have self-rule and was instead governed by men and women sent from Valyria to rule in the name of the Freehold.

entries.name: Oros
entries.description: Oros is a city that sits on the northern coast of the Smoking Sea in Essos, said to be second only in majesty to the city of Valyria. It lies to the south of the Lands of the Long Summer and is connected by Valyrian road to Mantarys, while across the Smoking Sea lies Tyria. Oros was founded by the Valyrian Freehold. Although rich and glorious, it did not have self-rule and was instead governed by men and women sent from Valyria to rule in the name of the Freehold.

entries.name: Ancient Valyria
entries.description: Ancient Valyria was a civilization of humble shepherds who discovered dragons in the Fourteen Flames. The Valyrians tamed the dragons with magic and mastered the technique of raising and training the dragons into devastating weapons of war. They began expanding their influence, establishing the Freehold with the city of Valyria as its capital. Magic flowered, topless towers rose toward the heavens where dragons soared, stone Valyrian sphinxes gazed down through eyes of garnet, and smiths used spells to forge Valyrian steel weapons of legendary strength and sharpness.

entries.name: Old Empire of Ghis
entries.description: The Old Empire of Ghis was one of the oldest known nations and cultures in the world before it was destroyed by the Valyrian Freehold. It reigned supreme over much of Essos. Its founding and golden age predate that of its successor, the Valyrian Freehold, by thousands of years. Five great Ghiscari wars were fought between Ghiscar and the Valyrian Freehold. The Ghiscari won some battles, but the Ghiscari eventually lost each war. The Old Empire fell in the Fifth Ghiscari War the Valyrians smashed the Ghiscari legions and used their dragons to burn Old Ghis and its pyramids to the ground. The Valyrians sowed the fields with salt and sulfur to prevent any surviving inhabitants from returning.

entries.name: Valyrian roads
entries.description: Valyrian roads, also called dragon roads, are broad stone highways built when the Valyrian Freehold dominated Essos. They are straight and usually run from one economic center to another, allowing swift transport of goods. Valyrian roads ran across much of the Valyrian peninsula, connecting the cities of Valyria, Tyria, and Oros with outlying settlements. The demon road runs from Meereen westward past Mantarys to Volantis on the Rhoyne; a branch of the demon road also runs south to Tolos near the Black Cliffs. A road continues north from Volantis to the ruins of Sar Mell. In northern Essos, a Valyrian road runs east from Pentos on the narrow sea to the ruins of Ghoyan Drohe in the Velvet Hills. From Ghoyan Drohe it runs northeast to Norvos and then southeast to Qohor. From the latter city a road connects to the ruins of Ar Noy to the southwest. A road continues east from Qohor to Essaria and Sarnath. Another road runs north from Essariato Saath on the Shivering Sea.

entries.name: Valyrian steel
entries.description: Valyrian steel is a type of steel from Valyria, used to make weapons and various other items of unparalleled quality. Magic plays a role in its forging, which makes the steel special and gives it magical characteristics. The properties of Valyrian steel are the result of both folding iron many times to balance and remove impurities, and the use of spells, giving unnatural strength to the resulting steel. Valyrian steel blades are lighter, stronger, harder, and sharper than the best castle-forged steel. The blades feature distinctive rippled patterns, the mark of steel that has been folded back on itself many thousands of times. Most Valyrian steel is dark grey in color, almost appearing black. No common fire, not even dragonflame, can damage Valyrian steel.

entries.name: Essaria
entries.description: Essaria was a colony of the Valyrian Freehold.

entries.name: Sarnath
entries.description: The greatest of the Tall Men cities, Sarnath was the seat of the High King of Sarnor, who dwelled in the fabled Palace With a Thousand Rooms.

entries.name: Tall Men
entries.description: The Tall Men, known as Tagaez Fen in their native language, are a people native to the grasslands of Essos. In Westeros they are known as the Sarnori, for at the height of their power the Kingdom of Sarnor ruled all the lands watered by the Sarne and the lakes that were once the Silver Sea, and fifty leagues beyond. Tall Men were long of limb, brown of skin, like the Zoqora, and with eyes and hair as black as night. Sarnori riders wore steel and spider silk, and rode coal-black mares, whilst the greatest of their warriors went to battle in scythed chariots pulled by teams of bloodred horses. These were often driven by their wives or daughters, for it was the custom among the Tall Men for men and women to make war together.

entries.name: Glass candle
entries.description: A glass candle is a candle made of obsidian, obsidian is called frozen fire by the Valyrians. These glass candles give off an unpleasantly bright light that does strange things to colors, white becomes as bright as fresh fallen snow, yellow shines like gold, reds turns to flame, and shadows become so black that they look like holes in the world. When the glass candles burned, the sorcerers of the Valyrian Freehold could see across mountains, seas, and deserts; give men visions and dreams; and communicate with one another half a world apart.

entries.name: Rhoynar
entries.description: The Rhoynar were a culture of river-faring people who dwelt on the banks of the immense river Rhoyne in Essos. After being forced to flee in ten thousand ships during the Rhoynish Wars with Valyria, the surviving Rhoynar eventually settled in Dorne in southern Westeros. The Rhoynar are a slender people with smooth olive skin, black hair, and dark eyes. The Rhoynar practiced a number of customs that differ from mainstream Andal culture. These included equal primogeniture, granting inheritances to the eldest child regardless of sex. They also tolerated homosexuality. Due to their origin in city-states, the Rhoynar titled their rulers Princes and Princesses. Their influence made these customs standard in Dorne as well. The Rhoynar worshipped a number of river-themed nature gods. Their primary god was Mother Rhoyne, or Mother River, the personification of the river Rhoyne itself. Other gods include the Old Man of the River, a turtle god, and his adversary, the Crab King. Art and music flourished in the ancient cities of the Rhoynar. They were by and large a peaceful people, but were fiercely independent, and could be formidable when roused to wroth.

entries.name: Rhoynish Wars
entries.description: The Rhoynish Wars were a series of wars fought between the city-states of the Rhoynar and colonies of the Valyrian Freehold. The last of the wars was the Second Spice War. In total, the series of conflicts spanned most of two and a half centuries.

entries.name: Second Spice War
entries.description: The Second Spice War was the last of the Rhoynish Wars between the Rhoynar and Valyria. The war began three dragonlords from the Valyrian Freehold joined Volantis in destroying the Rhoynish port Sarhoy on the Summer Sea. The Rhoynar responded by uniting under Prince Garin of Chroyane, the wonder of the Rhoyne who temporarily made Valyria tremble. Garin led a Rhoynish army of 250,000, which conquered Selhorys, Valysar, and Volon Therys, where they defeated three dragons with Rhoynish water wizards. The alarmed Volantenes sought help from Valyria itself, and the dragonlords responded by sending 300 dragons. The Valyrians crushed Garin's army with their dragons, then destroyed Sar Mell and Chroyane. Princess Nymeria of Ny Sar, seeing the fate of Garin and his army, gathered the surviving Rhoynar, most of whom were women and children and old men, aboard their remaining watercraft and fled from Essos aboard ten thousand ships. The city of Ghoyan Drohe on the Little Rhoyne was turned into a ruin by the Valyrian dragons. Other cities destroyed by the Valyrians were Ar Noy and Nymeria's Ny Sar.

entries.name: Andalos
entries.description: Andalos, also called the Hills of Andalos, is an area of northwestern Essos which was the homeland of the Andals. Due to migration and invasion, however, little is left of the original Andal culture.

entries.name: Andals
entries.description: The Andals are one of the three major ethnic groups from which the humans of Westeros descend, the others being the First Men and the Rhoynar. The Andal invasion caused the fall of many of the kingdoms of the First Men which had developed in the wake of the Pact with the children of the forest. The Andals are a tall and fair-haired people. The Andals fled because of the expanding Valyrian Freehold. The Valyrians established Myr in place of a walled Andal town and many of the Valyrian colonists of Pentos intermarried with local Andals. The Andals brought the Faith of the Seven to Westeros and with it the warrior tradition of the knight. The Andals used iron, while the First Men used bronze. The Andals also brought a superior writing system that supplanted the First Men's runes.

entries.name: Valysar
entries.description: Valysar is a walled colony of the Valyrian Freehold in Essos. It sits on the western bank of the Rhoyne, to the north of Volon Therys and to the south of Selhorys. Although it is a very large city, Valysar is considered a town.

entries.name: Selhorys
entries.description: Selhorys is a walled Volantene town and colony of the Valyrian Freehold, located at the confluence of the Selhoru and the lower Rhoyne in western Essos. It lies north of Valysar, northwest of Volantis, and south of Chroyane. Although it is very large city, Selhorys is still considered a town, not an independent city. Alone among the major towns, Selhorys stands upon the eastern bank of the Rhoyne. Selhorys has towers, domes, and cobbled paths. The city's sandstone walls shelter shops, stalls, and storehouses along the piers. The river gate is guarded by soldiers. Lanterns within the city are made of colored glass, unlike the parchment lanterns outside of the city walls. Pleasure houses and inns front the square, including a large stone inn with an immense turtle hanging above its door.

entries.name: Children of the forest
entries.description: The children of the forest, or Dryads, are a mysterious non-human race that inhabit the continent of Westeros during the Dawn Age long before the arrival of the First Men thousands of years ago. The giants call them woh dak nag gram (little squirrel people). They call themselves those who sing the song of earth in the True Tongue. The children are smaller than humans, but not childlike. They have nut-brown skin, dappled like a deer's with paler spots. Their hands have only three fingers and a thumb, with sharp black claws instead of nails. They have large ears that can hear things that no man can hear. They usually have large gold and green eyes slitted like those of a cat, allowing them to see in dark passages. The children are slight, quick, and graceful. They weave leaves and vines and flowers into their hair, and wear cloaks of leaves. They live for centuries. They often sing in their language, the True Tongue. Very rarely, one of the children is born with mossy green or blood red eyes, a sign that they have been chosen by the Old Gods. The chosen ones are not robust, and do not live long on the earth, but they have the gift of greensight and are known as greenseers. Once they are bound to a weirwood, they live far longer than other children. The children are omnivores as they feed on different types of food they find and cultivate. The children live in clans. They do not use metal, weave cloth, or build cities. The children lived off the land, using stone and obsidian implements, wearing bark leg-bindings and shirts of woven leaves, dwelling in caves, crannogs, and hidden tree villages. Males and females both hunted side by side as wood dancers, using obsidian weapons, weirwood bows, and flying snares made with grasses. The children had no books, no ink, no parchment and no written language. They are a people with a deep connection to the land. The Dryads also use powerful magic. The children of the forest are gifted with supernatural powers. These included having power over the beasts of the wood, the ability to wear an animal's skin, the skill to create music so beautiful as to bring tears to the eyes of any who heard it, the greensight ability and the ability to speak to the dead. It was the children who carved faces on weirwoods to keep watch over the woods. The children of the forest believed that the weirwood trees were gods, and when they died they became a part of them.

entries.name: Weirwood
entries.description: The five-pointed leaves and the sap of weirwoods are blood-red, while the smooth bark on their wide trunks and wood are bone white. Most weirwoods have faces carved into their trunks. This was done by the children of the forest. In some cases sap has collected in the crevices of the carved faces, giving the trees red eyes which have been known to drip sap as if the trees were weeping. A weirwood will live forever if undisturbed.

entries.name: Giants
entries.description: Giants are a race of sentient humanoids that once lived in various regions of the known world, but now live only in northern parts of Westeros. The people of Westeros believe them to be extinct. Giants generally grow between ten to fourteen feet tall. They are capable of great feats of strength. They are covered by a shaggy pelt of fur, that is thicker below their waists than above. The fur of older giants becomes grey and streaked with white. Their heads are thrust forward from their shoulder blades. They have squashed-in faces with square teeth, and tiny eyes. Their eyesight is poor, and they snuffle constantly, smelling as much as they see. Giants have sloped chests, and their lower torsos are about half again as wide as their upper torsos. Their arms hang lower than a man's, while their legs are shorter than their arms, ending in splayed and horny feet that need no shoes even in the coldest weather. Female giants look similar to males, both being bearded. While hostile to men, giants are a shy folk who use little technology. They wield huge clubs that are often no more than logs, though some tie boulders to the end to make crude mauls or use huge stone axes. Giants ride mammoths as steeds and are protective of the animals. Giants speak the Old Tongue of the First Men, referring to children of the forest as woh dak nag gran, or "little squirrel people". Giants do not have kings. giants are vegetarians. Giants roam freely, and reside beneath tall trees or in caverns.

entries.name: Bone Mountains
entries.description: The Bone Mountains are a colossal mountain range in central Essos. The tallest mountains in the known world, they are a natural land barrier between the western part of Essos known to Westerosi and the exotic, mysterious Further East of the continent. The Bone Mountains stretch longitudinally across five hundred leagues, beginning east of Qarth in the south by the Summer Sea. The southernmost Bones are called the Dry Bones because of their lack of water. The Bones north of the Steel Road extends north through the Realm of the Jhogwin to the Shivering Sea. The Bones cross one hundred leagues from east to west. While there are hundreds of visible and hidden paths through the Bones, there are only three routes large enough for armies. The Steel Road, the most northerly route, cuts between the Krazaaj Zasqa to Kayakayanaya, then skirts around the top of the Great Sand Sea and south to Trader Town. The Stone Road is the middle route from Yinishar to Samyriana. The Sand Road, the southerly route, begins at Qarth, heads north through the red waste, and cuts through the Dry Bones to Bayasabhad and Tiqui.

entries.name: Yinishar
entries.description: Yinishar is a city in Essos, located on the Stone Road in the foothills of the western Bone Mountains. Yinishar is inhabited by people related to those of Samyriana. Yinishar is located along the Silk Road.

entries.name: Volantis
entries.description: Volantis, often called the First Daughter, is a city in southwestern Essos. Located at the mouth of the Rhoyne on the Summer Sea, it is the oldest and the proudest of the Valyrian colonies. Volantis is one of the greatest, richest, and most powerful of these city-states. Established to protect the borders of the Freehold, Volantis grew powerful trading with Valyria and the Rhoynar, although the nearby Rhoynish city Sarhoy declined. This led to the Rhoynish Wars. Volantis is a port city. Its large, deep harbor is ideally placed. Volantis spreads across the mouth of the Rhoyne and across the hills and marshes on both sides of the river. The older districts of the city lie upon the eastern banks, while the newer districts are located on the west. These two halves are connected by the Long Bridge. The Black Walls of eastern Volantis protect a large labyrinth of palaces, courtyards, towers, temples, cloisters, bridges, and cellars, and where the Valyrian Nobles reside in their palaces. The Black Walls are a great oval of fused black dragonstone, harder than steel or diamond, built two hundred feet high by the Valyrian Freehold. The Long Bridge joins the two halves of Volantis across the mouth of the Rhoyne. Its gateway is an arch of black stone carved with sphinxes, manticores, dragons, and other beasts. No outlander, freeman, or foreigner is allowed inside the Black Wall unless they are invited by the Valyrian Nobles.

entries.name: Tyrosh
entries.description: Tyrosh is a harbor city and one of the Free Cities. It is on an island to the north of the Stepstones. Tyrosh began as a military outpost of the Valyrian Freehold on a bleak stony isle to control shipping through the Stepstones. They soon discovered in the nearby waters a unique variety of sea snail whose secretions were used to create a dye popular with Valyrian nobles. Thousands of merchants developed Tyrosh into a major city within a generation. Tyroshi dyers learned to produce different colors of dyes by varying the diet of the snails. Tyrosh, a fortress city protected by high walls, is on the northernmost and easternmost of the Stepstones. Its inner walls are fused black dragonstone. At the mouth of its harbor lies the Bleeding Tower. Like Lys, Tyrosh has pleasure houses.

entries.name: Lys
entries.description: Lys, known as Lys the Lovely, is one of the Valyrian Colonies of Essos. It is a small city clinging to rocks surrounded by stormy seas. The city lies off to the southeast of Tyrosh and to the west of Volantis. The term "Lyseni" is both singular and plural, and "Lysene" as an adjective. Lys was founded as a colony of the Valyrian Freehold. Founded by wealthy Valyrian merchants and nobles. Due to its climate, Lys soon became a resort destination of sorts for the dragonlords of Valyria, and is considered a paradise. The sunny island is fertile with palm and fruit trees, and the surrounding blue-green waters are filled with fish. Lys is protected by high walls and soldiers. The city is known for its pillow houses and pleasure gardens, training slaves in the arts of love and selling them as concubines and bed-slaves.

entries.name: Myr
entries.description: Myr is one of the Valyrian Colonies of Essos. It is on the east shore of the Sea of Myrth. Myr was founded by merchant adventurers from the Valyrian Freehold after they conquered a walled Andal town. Walled Myr is on the fertile "heel" of Essos, where an Valyrian dragonroad on the mainland meets the Sea of Myrth. Some Myrmen are descended from the Rhoynar, as some of the Myrmen share their olive skin and dark hair. Myrmen speak a dialect of bastard Valyrian with a Myrish accent can sound sultry.

entries.name: Archon
entries.description: Archons were provisionally elected by and from the lords freeholder of Valyria. Often dragonriders, archons from Valyria oversaw colonial cities and towns of the Valyrian Freehold, with the exceptions of the self-ruling Valyrian colony cities.

entries.name: Great Empire of the Dawn
entries.description: The Great Empire of the Dawn was a mythic realm established on all the land between the Bones and the Grey Waste, from the Shivering Sea to the Jade Sea and including the isle of Leng, and the predecessor to the Golden Empire of Yi Ti. According to legend, the Golden Empire's first ruler was the God-on-Earth, the only son of the Lion of Night and the Maiden-Made-of-Light, who traveled in a palanquin carved from a single pearl and carried by a hundred queens, his wives. He ruled for ten thousand years until he ascended to the stars to join his forebears. Dominion then passed to his eldest son, the Pearl Emperor, who ruled for a thousand years. Power then passed to the Jade Emperor, the Tourmaline Emperor, the Onyx Emperor, the Topaz Emperor, and the Opal Emperor. Each reigning for a shorter and more troubled time than the previous emperor, for wild men and beasts pressed the borders of the Empire, lesser kings grew proud and rebellious, and the common people gave themselves to sin. When the daughter of the Opal Emperor ascended to power as the Amethyst Empress, her envious brother cast her down and proclaimed himself the Bloodstone Emperor and began a reign of terror and slavery, in which he practiced dark arts and necromancy, took a tiger-woman for his bride, feasted on human flesh and cast down the gods of Yi Ti to worship a black stone fallen from the sky. This Blood Betrayal ushered in the Long Night, with the Maiden-Made-of-Light turning her back on the world, while the Lion of Night came forth to punish the wickedness of man. The darkness ended when a great warrior rose to lead the virtuous into battle with the sword Lightbringer in his hand. Light was restored, but the Great Empire was not reborn for the restored world was a broken place where every tribe of men went its own way, fearful of all the others, and war, lust, and murder had endured.

entries.name: The Long Night
entries.description: The Long Night is a period when a terrible darkness fell across the known world. It occurred during the Age of Heroes, in the midst of a great winter that lasted for years. The Long Night lasted a generation and laid waste through famine and terror.

entries.name: Golden Empire of Yi Ti
entries.description: The Golden Empire of Yi Ti is a realm located in the eponymous region of the Further East of Essos. It is the supposed successor to the mythic Great Empire of the Dawn, which, according to legend, fell during the Long Night. It is ruled by a God-Emperor, who is worshiped as divine, though in the present day the God-Emperor has little actual power beyond the limits of the capital city. Throughout the centuries, the capital Golden Empire has constantly moved as dynasties rose and fell. From Yin, on the shores of the Jade Sea, To the fallen city of Si Qo in the heart of the jungle, or at Jinqi. The current capital is Yin, where the seventeenth azure emperor Bu Gai keeps his court.

entries.name: God-on-Earth
entries.description: The God-on-Earth was the legendary first ruler of the mythic Great Empire of the Dawn. According to the tales told by the priestly scribes of Yin, he was the only begotten son of the Maiden-Made-of-Light and the Lion of Night, and traveled about his domains in a palanquin carved from a single pearl and carried by a hundred queens, his wives. He ruled for ten thousand years, in which the empire flourished, until at last he ascended to the stars to join his forebears. He was succeeded by his eldest son, the Pearl Emperor.

entries.name: Maiden-Made-of-Light
entries.description: The Maiden-Made-of-Light is a goddess in Yi Ti. According to tales told by the priestly scribes of Yin, the Maiden-Made-of-Light was impregnated by the Lion of Night. This son was the God-on-Earth, who ruled the Great Empire of the Dawn for ten thousand year before ascending to the heavens. The descendants of the God-Earth ruled the empire after him, each ruling a shorter time than the previous one, until the brother of the Amethyst Empress usurped her in the Blood Betrayal and crowned himself as the Bloodstone Emperor, ushering in the Long Night. The Maiden-Made-of-Light turned her back upon the world and the Lion of Night came forth in all his wroth to punish the wickedness of man.

entries.name: Magic
entries.description: Magic is a supernatural force in the known world. It is rare enough for many to doubt its effectiveness or even existence in Westeros and especially in the Oldtown, where it is known as the higher mysteries. Valyrians are the most learned in the arts of Magic. All manner of wizards, sorcerers, necromancers, spellsingers, aeromancers, bloodmages, and more are said to gather and practice their arts in the lands by the Jade Sea and Asshai.

entries.name: Dragonglass
entries.description: Dragonglass is the name used by smallfolk for a volcanic glass which maesters of the Citadel call obsidian. The Valyrians called it frozen fire. Obsidian is volcanic glass formed by immense heat and pressure in the earth. Obsidian was used by the children of the forest to fabricate weapons; obsidian blades are sharper than steel but far more brittle. The Valyrians use obsidian to make their glass candles. Dragonglass weapons are one of the few weaknesses of the Others.

entries.name: Norvos
entries.description: Norvos is one of the Valyrian Colonies of Essos. It lies in the interior of Essos, between Pentos and Qohor. Norvos, like Qohor and Lorath, was founded following a religious schism in the Valyrian Freehold. Dissidents found the religious tolerance of the Freehold intolerable, so the sect of the bearded priests founded Norvos as a theocracy where the "true faith" would be practiced. Norvos is located in a land of rolling hills and terraced farms, surrounded by small walled villages. Norvos is made up out of two parts, joined only by a massive stone stair, known as the Sinner's Steps. The high city, where the ancient nobility of Norvos lives, is ringed about by mighty stone walls, and located on the tallest hill in the region. Here, the great fortress-temple of the bearded priests is located. The lower city is located three hundred feet below, at the base of the hill, by the river, spread out along the muddy shores. It is defended by moats, ditches, and a timber palisade, overgrown with moss. The riverfront is lined with wharves, brothels, and beer halls. While the upper city is grim, the lower city is lively. Norvos is a theocracy. While it has a council of magisters, its members are chosen by the bearded priests, who speak for their god and wield the true power in the Free City.

entries.name: Pentos.Pentoshi
entries.description: Pentos is one of the Valyrian Colonies of western Essos. It is a port located on the eastern coast of the Bay of Pentos. Pentos was founded by merchants, traders, seafarers, and farmers from the Valyrian Freehold as a trading outpost. Many were smallfolk who bred with local Andals, so the Pentoshi are less protective of Valyrian blood than other Free Cities. Pentos grew to control almost all of Andalos, with domains stretching from the Velvet Hills and the Little Rhoyne to the narrow sea. Even though Pentos has massive, high walls, it is often regarded as the most vulnerable of the Free Cities. The city has many square brick towers. Most of the roofing is done in tiles. Pentos has walled estates. The Sunrise Gate allows the traveller to exit the city to the east, in the direction of the Rhoyne. Pentoshi are great lovers of song, and generous with those who please them.

entries.name: Qohor
entries.description: Qohor is one of the easternmost Valyrian Colonies of western Essos. The initial settlement of Qohor was a lumber camp along the Forest of Qohor. Qohor was colonized by followers of the Black Goat. The religious dissidents abandoned Valyria, rejecting the religious tolerance practiced by the Valyrian Freehold. Qohor is the most exotic of the Free Cities, due to its status as the western terminus for overland trade networks stretching all the way to Yi Ti. The dark arts, such as divination, blood magic, and necromancy, are are also practiced in the City.

entries.name: The Black Goat
entries.description: The Black Goat is the main god worshipped in the Free City of Qohor. The Black Goat demands daily blood sacrifice. The Qohorik often bring calves, bullocks, and horses before the Black Goat's altars. However, on holy days it is condemned criminals who go beneath the knives of the god's cowled priests, and, in times of danger and crisis it is written that the high nobles of the city offer their own children to placate the Black Goat, that he might defend the city.

entries.name: Braavos
entries.description: Braavos is a secret and powerful of the Free Cities. It is located in the Great Lagoon on the northwestern end of Essos, where the narrow sea and the Shivering Sea meet. Braavos is known as the Secret City. Braavos is sometimes referred to as the "bastard daughter of Valyria." Braavos is not part of the Valyrian Freehold. Braavos is founded by escaped slaves, fleeing the grasp of the Freehold. The slaves travelled to the distant lagoon, hidden away from sight of the dragonlords by the wall of hills covered with pine trees and the fog covering the lagoon.
