The founders of Braavos risked their lives for freedom, and swore a vow that no one in their city would ever be a slave, thrall, or bondsman. This vow became the First Law of Braavos, and is engraved on the arch spanning the Long Canal. Braavos is comprised of a hundred islands linked together by small stone bridges spanning the many canals throughout the city. The houses in the humbler regions are tightly packed together, even over the canals. There are no trees to be found within the city (except in the courts and gardens of the mighty). Braavos is a flat city of stone architecture and granite monuments. The houses are usually slim buildings with peaked tile roofs, raised four to five stories tall. The Braavosi are a kind people, great lovers of song. Instead of traveling by horse, the Braavosi use boats. The Braavosi tongue is a bastard version of High Valyrian. Braavosi culture has created a unique form of sword fighting, the water dance. The style is a refined form of fencing in which the practitioner stands sideways and wields a slender blade. Braavos has courtesans. Every courtesan has her own barge and servants to work them. Songs are sung about them, and they are showered with gifts from goldsmiths and craftsmen beg for their custom.

entries.name: Westeros
entries.description: Westeros is home to seven independent Kingdoms. The closest foreign nations to Westeros are the Free Cities, a collection of independent city-states across the narrow sea in western Essos. To the south of Westeros lie the Summer Isles. The continent of Westeros is long and relatively narrow, extending from Dorne in the south to the lands beyond the Wall. In the far north are the frozen Lands of Always Winter, where a large amount of land remains uncharted due to the extremely cold temperatures. Westeros's eastern coast borders on the narrow sea; across those waters lies the eastern continent of Essos and the island chain known as the Stepstones. To the south is located the Summer Sea, and within it the Summer Isles. The seven independent Kingdoms are Kingdom in the North, Kingdom of the Isles and the Rivers, Kingdom of Mountain and Vale, Kingdom of the Rock, Kingdom of the Reach, Kingdom of the Storm, and Realm of Dorne.

entries.name: Kingdom of the North
entries.description: Kingdom of the North, or the winterlands, is one seven independent Kingdoms of Westeros ruled by Kings in the North. The largest region of the Seven Kingdoms. The north has been ruled by the Starks for thousands of years from the castle known as Winterfell. The only city in the region is White Harbor, while the most prominent northern towns are the winter town and Barrowton. Notable bannermen of the region include Bolton, Cerwyn, Dustin, Flint, Glover, Hornwood, Karstark, Manderly, Mormont, Reed, Ryswell, Tallhart, and Umber. Bastards of noble origin raised in the north are given the surname Snow. Most northmen are descended from the First Men, although there have been centuries of intermarriage with the Andals south of the Neck. The Old Tongue spoken by the First Men of antiquity has been replaced in the north by the Common Tongue. Northern accents can be considered "frosted". Many northmen are large in stature and have thick beards, long hair, and heavy cloaks of wool or fur. Northern warriors can ride shaggy horses. Many northmen disapprove of tourneys and gambling. Guest right is treasured in the north. Northmen have long memories and seek rightful vengeance when wronged. A northern custom is that he who passes that sentence should swing the sword. Most of the north's people still follow the old gods and their heart trees, and have little inclination for newer religions. Northmen hold the Night's Watch in high regard, and many lords send annual gifts to support the black brothers. The first night is a a marriage tradition practiced in the North. When smallfolk marry, their lord or king has the privilege to bed the bride on the first night. During harsh winters, many farmers and younger northmen seek refuge in the winter town or at the castles of lords.

entries.name: Kingdom of the Isles and the Rivers
entries.description: Kingdom of the Isles and the Rivers is one seven independent Kingdoms of Westeros ruled by House Hoare, their realm included both the Iron Islands and the riverlands. House Hoare conquered the Trident from the Storm King. House Hoare ruled from a tower house at Fairmarket, while Harren the Black constructed the massive castle of Harrenhal along the Gods Eye.
keywords: kingdom of the isles and the rivers

entries.name: House Hoare
entries.description: House Hoare of Orkmont is an house originally from the Iron Islands. The Hoares became Kings of the Iron Islands after Andal settlers on the islands ended the rule of House Greyiron. The Hoares eventually moved to Fairmarket and Harrenhal in the riverlands, where they ruled as Kings of the Isles and the Rivers for three generations. The Hoare banner depicted per saltire and with two heavy silver chains crossing between a gold longship on black, a dark green pine on white, a cluster of red grapes on gold, and a black raven flying in a blue sky. Hoares traits are ungodly, they have black of hair, black of eye, and black of hearts. The Hoare kings are cunning and cruel, but not valorous.

entries.name: Riverlands
entries.description: The riverlands, historically the Kingdom of Rivers and Hills, are a central region of Westeros, consisting of the rich, fertile, and populous areas around the three forks of the Trident and the northern Blackwater Rush. They were once ruled by native river kings for centuries earlier. Because of their central position in Westeros and lack of natural boundaries, the riverlands have been a frequent battleground. The people of the riverlands are known as "rivermen" or occasionally "riverlanders", and they are a mixture of hardy warriors, peaceful fisherfolk, and devout smallfolk. Their lords have a reputation for being notoriously quarrelsome, and are referred to as "river lords". Noble bastards born in the riverlands are given the surname Rivers. The riverlands encompass a region of plains, forests, hills, and endless rivers, and borders on every single kingdom except Dorne. Their northern border is near the swamplands of the Neck, the southernmost region of the north. To the east is the Vale of Arryn's Mountains. To the south the riverlands border the Reach. The riverlands do not contain any major cities, but have a number of towns. The Faith of the Seven has become the most common religion in the riverlands. There are several septries in the territory, and many septs and motherhouses. The Faith Militant is strong among the rivermen, and Stoney Sept is known for its chapter of Warrior's Sons. Unlike most river lords, House Blackwood continue to follow the old gods of the First Men. Guest right is an important custom in the riverlands. The quarrelsome river lords have a fractious history. The green men tend to the weirwoods on the Isle of Faces within the Gods Eye, which is rarely visited by anyone from the mainland. Notable houses of the region have included Blackwood, Bracken, Darry, Frey, Lothston, Mallister, Mooton, Mudd, Piper, Ryger, Strong, Vance, and Whent.

entries.name: Stoney Sept
entries.description: Stoney Sept is a walled town in the southern riverlands. It is located south of Acorn Hall, southeast of Pinkmaiden, and north of the Goldroad. The headwaters of the Blackwater Rush are nearby. The heart of Stoney Sept is a market square with a fountain in the shape of a leaping trout. A brothel known as the Peach is located on the east side of the market. The town's namesake old sept sits on a hill. Below it is a stout holdfast made of grey stone. There are many bells in Stoney Sept, including bronze bells and silver chimes.

entries.name: Isle of Faces
entries.description: The Isle of Faces is a sacred island in the middle of the lake called the Gods Eye, located in the southeastern riverlands. It is one of the few known locations of weirwoods in the south of Westeros, with most others having been cut down and burned. The green men are a sacred order entrusted with the guardianship of the Isle of Faces in the riverlands. Some nursery tales claim they are horned and have dark, green skin. Most maesters believe their clothes are green and they wear headdresses with horns.

entries.name: Iron Islands
entries.description: The Iron Islands, the Iron Isles, or the Kingdom of the Iron Isles, is one of the constituent regions of Westeros. The isles are ruled by rock, salt, and High Kings chosen in kingsmoots, next by hereditary Kings of the Iron Islands, and then briefly by Kings of the Isles and the Rivers. The Iron Islands are home to a fierce seafaring people who call themselves the ironborn. While some say the archipelago is named after the abundant iron ore on the islands, the ironborn claim it is instead named after their own unyielding nature. It is often said that every captain is a king aboard his own ship, so the islands are also called "the land of ten thousand kings". The Iron Islands is an archipelago in Ironman's Bay, located in the Sunset Sea off the western coast of Westeros. They are roughly west of the riverlands, northwest of the westerlands, and south of the north. The main grouping of islands numbers thirty-one, with the seven major isles being Pyke, Great Wyk, Old Wyk, Harlaw, Saltcliffe, Blacktyde, and Orkmont. Eight days sail northwest of Great Wyk is a smaller grouping of thirteen clustered around the Lonely Light. Some of the Iron Islands are used for sheep grazing or are uninhabited. The ironborn are independent, fierce, and sometimes cruel. They live in a harsh land and hold no love for the peoples of the mainland Westeros, whom they consider weak. Ironborn culture allows for one rock wife and multiple salt wives, and they prefer to have thralls perform manual labor. The Faith of the Seven and the old gods find small favor with the ironborn, as their allegiance is given to their native Drowned God. Ironmen who often sail to the mainland are more likely to have maesters, singers, and knights in their retinues. Most ironmen believe in the way of reaving and paying the iron price. Notable houses have included Blacktyde, Botley, Drumm, Goodbrother, Greyiron, Harlaw, Hoare, Merlyn, Stonehouse, Sunderly, Tawney, and Wynch. Bastards of noble origin from the Iron Islands receive the surname Pyke.

entries.name: Iron price
entries.description: The iron price in ironborn culture refers to warriors acquiring possessions by taking them by force from defeated adversaries, rather than purchasing items with currency, which they refer to as the gold price. Thralls and salt wives can be acquired only through reaving, never through transactions.

entries.name: Kingsmoot
entries.description: Kingsmoots were great councils held by inhabitants of the Iron Islands in which kings were chosen by longship captains. The kingsmoots which chose the High King of the Iron Islands were held on Nagga's Hill on Old Wyk. Any captain who owns a ship may participate when a kingsmoot is held. Candidates may try to sway his fellow captains with a speech on his prowess and gifts to show his generosity; only once a vast majority call out a candidate's name to proclaim him king does the kingsmoot end.

entries.name: Nagga's hill
entries.description: Nagga's hill is located on the isle of Old Wyk in the Iron Islands. The hill overlooks Nagga's Cradle, the body of water between Old Wyk and Great Wyk. Forty-four stone ribs of Nagga, a dead sea dragon, rise from the ground like large white trees as wide as a dromond's mast and twice as tall.

entries.name: Old Wyk
entries.description: Old Wyk is one of the islands that make up the Iron Islands. Considered the holiest of the isles. Lord Dunstan Drumm is known as the Lord of Old Wyk. Located in Ironman's Bay and inhabited by the ironborn, Old Wyk is found north and east of Great Wyk and west of Orkmont. Windy hills and black mountains make up much of Old Wyk, and Nagga's hill and the ruins of the Grey King's Hall are located on it near Nagga's Cradle. Shatterstone, the seat of the Goodbrothers of Old Wyk, is located by the island's coast.

entries.name: Faith of the Seven
entries.description: The Faith of the Seven, also referred to as the Holy Faith or simply the Faith, is the dominant religion in most of Westeros. Followers of the Faith are rare in the north and on the Iron Islands. The gods of the Faith are known as the new gods to differentiate them from the old gods of the First Men. Members of the Faith worship the Seven, a single deity with seven aspects or faces. For the less educated, this concept is often difficult to grasp, causing them to often believe that there are seven different gods. The seven faces are The Father, The Mother, The Warrior, The Smith, The Maiden, The Crone, and the Stranger. The male and female godsworn of the Faith are called septons and septas, respectively. Upon taking their vows, they set aside their last names. The head of the Faith is the High Septon, who is elected by a council of the high-ranking septons. The silent sisters are tasked with preparing the deceased for the grave. Humbler members of the Faith are "holy brothers" and "holy sisters". The Faith Militant is the military arm of the Faith of the Seven. The Faith hold its own ecclesiastical courts to try servants of the Faith accused of wrongdoing. The Faith's wealth and properties are exempt from taxation. The sacred courts sit in judgment of kings and queens. Teachings of the Faith have a heavy influence on Westeros. The Faith preaches against prostitution, gambling, and bastardy. It holds slavery, polygamy, incest and prostitution as monstrous and vile sins. Religious worship is done in septs. The Faith holds that there are seven heavens and seven hells. Although all sins may be forgiven, crimes must still be punished. The Lord of the Seven Hells is said to command demons and practice black arts. Holding hands and singing is part of worship and prayer. The Faith has a number of holy books. The most important one is The Seven-Pointed Star.

entries.name: Faith Militant
entries.description: The Faith Militant is the military arm of the Faith of the Seven. It was composed of two military orders, the Warrior's Sons and the Poor Fellows, known as the "Swords" and the "Stars" for their respective symbols.

entries.name: Warrior's Sons
entries.description: The Noble and Puissant Order of the Warrior's Sons is an order of Westerosi knights sworn to the Faith of the Seven. They are part of the Faith Militant, and are also known as the Swords. The Warrior's Sons obey and answer to the High Septon, as they believe the High Septon speaks for the Seven. Their symbol is a rainbow sword on black. The Warrior's Sons wore rainbow cloaks and inlaid silver armor over hair shirts. They bore star-shaped crystals in the pommels of their longswords. They have crystals adorning the pommels of their longswords and the crests of their greathelms, and carry kite shields displaying their symbol. Their armor is made of silver plate, and polished to a mirror sheen. The Warrior's Sons are all anointed knights. Upon joining the Warrior's Sons, they take vows, giving up their lands and gold. The Warrior's Sons are permanently stationed at chapterhouses in several major cities and towns. The Warrior's Sons had one overall commander known as a Grand Captain.
aliases: Noble and Puissant Order of the Warrior's Sons
keywords: noble and puissant order of the warrior's sons

entries.name: Poor Fellows
entries.description: The Poor Fellows is an order of Westerosi, mostly smallfolk, sworn to the Faith of the Seven. They are part of the Faith Militant, they used a red seven-pointed star as their badge. The Poor Fellows obeyed and answered to the High Septon, as they believed the High Septon spoke for the Seven. Poor Fellows defend of wayfarers on the road, escorting pilgrims between septs. They greatly outnumbered their knightly counterparts in the Faith Militant, the Warrior's Sons. The Poor Fellows are of a humbler social background than the Warrior's Sons. Women could rise to be leaders of the Poor Fellows. Despite not being as trained, disciplined, or well-armed as the Warrior's Sons, the Poor Fellows formed the bulk of the Faith's army. They are lightly-armed footmen who carried whatever weapons they could make or find, often axes or cudgels, and they wore star badges, red on surcoats bleached white. Some even scourged or branded the seven-pointed star in their flesh.

entries.name: Septry
entries.description: A septry is a monastic community of men sworn to the Faith of the Seven. Brown brothers live in penitence, quiet contemplation, and prayer at septries, often taking a vow of silence. The leader of the community bears the title of Elder Brother, and he is assisted by proctors.

entries.name: Motherhouse
entries.description: A motherhouse is a monastic community of the Faith of the Seven for septas, silent sisters, and novices similar to a convent. The leader of the community bears the title of Mother.

entries.name: Sept
entries.description: A sept is a place of worship for followers of the Faith of the Seven. They can be found in villages and urban settlements, castles, septries and motherhouses. A sept is a single building with seven walls. Some septs are small and humble, but others are large and magnificent. Some septs have crystal or leaded windows. Ceremonies are led by the highest ranking male member of the clergy, and hymns are often sung. In the naming of a child, seven oils are used to anoint the infant. Weddings are conducted standing between the altars of the Father and the Mother. Knights traditionally stand vigil and are consecrated with seven oils in septs. Brothers of the Night's Watch who worship the Seven can make their vows at the small sept at Castle Black. As they are considered holy places, bloodshed is forbidden in septs.

entries.name: Silent sisters
entries.description: The silent sisters, also referred to as the handmaidens of the Stranger, are an order of women belonging to the Faith of the Seven. They are sworn to the service of the Stranger and have taken vows of chastity and silence. The silent sisters attend to the dead. They dress in grey robes, their faces hooded and shawled so only their eyes remain visible, as it is "ill fortune to look on the face of death." The silent sisters remove the bowels and organs, and drain the blood from the corpses in their care. They may also stuff the body with fragrant herbs and salts to preserve it and hide the smell of decomposition. When the deceased is transported back home, one or more silent sisters might accompany the body.

entries.name: Begging brother
entries.description: Begging brothers are mendicant holy men who serve the Faith of the Seven. Begging brothers often wear robes of undyed wool belted with hempen ropes. While septons wear a crystal about their neck on a leather thong, begging brothers instead have a bowl.

entries.name: Septon
entries.description: Septons are an order of men who serve as priests for the Faith of the Seven. Septons can study at great centers of religious training, but not all local septons are well educated. Upon taking his vows, a septon sets aside his last name. Septons often wear white robes, seven-stranded belts of different colors, and a crystal about their necks. Septons can perform holy services, marriages, and forgive sins. When a man becomes a knight, it is customary to stand a vigil and be anointed by a septon before reciting the knightly vows. While many septons serve at a single sept in villages, towns, cities, or castles, there are hundreds of traveling septons who provide services for poor villages.

entries.name: Septa
entries.description: Septas are an order of women godsworn to the Faith of the Seven. Women who wish to become septas train first as novices. Upon taking her vows, a septa sets aside her last name and take a vow of chastity. Septas often serve at motherhouses and in cloisters. They typically dress in white robes, some with a woven seven-color belt. Septas wear a crystal pendant about their necks. Septas teach girls how to read, write, do sums, and teach about piety, deportment, and the Faith. Many serve as governesses in noble households, teaching girls womanly arts. Septas serve as chaperones and guardians when their female charges keep company with men. Septas can receive confession from believers. Septas who copy and illuminate texts for the Faith are known to alter or remove texts they deem unacceptable.

entries.name: Kingdom of the Rock
entries.description: King of the Rock is one seven independent Kingdoms of Westeros ruled by House Lannister, who ruled the western hills and valleys of Westeros that is now the westerlands. The capital of the Kingdom of the Rock is Casterly Rock near Lannisport.

entries.name: Westerlands
entries.description: The westerlands is a region in the west of the continent of Westeros. People from the westerlands are known as westermen. The customary surname of bastards of noble origin born in the westerlands is Hill. The westerlands are known for their rugged hills, rolling plains, fertile fields, and broadleaf forests. The land contains lakes and rivers, and the hills conceal systems of caves and caverns. The region lies along the coast of the Sunset Sea, with Ironman's Bay and the Iron Islands to the north. Also along the coast is Casterly Rock, the seat of House Lannister. Near the Rock is Lannisport. The headwaters of the Tumblestone and the Red Fork begin in the westerlands and flow east into the riverlands. The main pass through the eastern hills is guarded by the Golden Tooth, a castle which controls access to the river road leading to Riverrun. The southern westerlands contain more flatland than the rest of the country. The south leads to the Reach. The westerlands are dotted with mines from which pour gold and silver in astonishing quantities. Notable bannermen have included Banefort, Brax, Broom, Clegane, Crakehall, Farman, Lefford, Lydden, Marbrand, Payne, Prester, Reyne, Serrett, Swyft, Tarbeck, and Westerling.

entries.name: Kingdom of the Reach
entries.description: Kingdom of the Reach is one seven independent Kingdoms of Westeros ruled by House Gardener, and their consorts were known as Queens of All the Reach, who rule the land of the Reach. The capital of the Kingdom of the Reach is Highgarden and the heart of chivalry in Westeros. It is the second-largest of the kingdoms behind the north and is considered the most fertile and heavily-populated part of Westeros.

entries.name: The Reach
entries.description: The Reach, or the Green Realm, is one of the constituent regions of the Seven Kingdoms on the continent of Westeros. It's ruled by the Kings and Queens of the Reach and is the most fertile and heavily-populated part of Westeros. The Reach is considered the home of chivalry in Westeros. It is the place where knighthood is looked upon with the greatest reverence and esteemed the most. It is also the place where the rules for tourneys are the most stringent and managed. The Reach is the most fertile part of Westeros and has numerous and well-populated villages and towns. The Sunset Sea is found to the west, while the hills of the westerlands are to the northwest and the Blackwater Rush of the riverlands is to the north. The Reach borders the stormlands to the northeast, while to the east and southeast are the stormlands and their Dornish Marches. South of the Reach are the Red Mountains of Dorne and the Summer Sea. The Reach is watered by the immense river Mander and its tributaries. The Reach proper is centered around the Mander. Oldtown is located at the mouth of the Honeywine. The region also includes several islands, including the Shield Islands near the mouth of the Mander and the Arbor. The Reach is the second wealthiest region in Westeros behind the westerlands. Among the products it produces are melons, fireplums, peaches, apples, and grapes. The Arbor makes the finest of rich wines, from reds to a golden vintage. Bride and groom traditionally exchange gifts on the morning of their wedding in the Reach. The golden coins of the Reach were known as hands. Notable houses have included Ashford, Caswell, Crane, Florent, Fossoway, Gardener, Hightower, Merryweather, Mullendore, Oakheart, Redwyne, Rowan, Tarly, and Vyrwel. Noble bastards born in the Reach are given the surname Flowers.

entries.name: House Gardener
entries.description: House Gardener of Highgarden is the famed house and Kings of the Reach. Beginning with the mythical first king Garth the Gardener, the Gardeners ruled, through war and peace and the assimilation with the Andals through the generations. The kings of House Gardener initially ruled the Reach proper, focused on Highgarden and the Mander river, but over time claimed supremacy over neighboring kings and lords. Their seat is Highgarden, where many rulers sat upon a living throne called the Oakenseat. The Gardener rulers wear crowns of vines and flowers when at peace, and crowns of iron thorns when they rode to war. Their blazon was a green hand over a white field.

entries.name: Garth the Gardener
entries.description: Garth Greenhand, also called Garth Greenhair and Garth the Green, was a mythical High King of the First Men said to have been the common ancestor of numerous houses from the Reach. His firstborn son, Garth the Gardener, founded House Gardener, the Kings of the Reach. Garth supposedly wore a crown of vines and flowers and made the land bloom. It is unclear if he is related to the First King.

entries.name: High Tower
entries.description: The Hightower or High Tower is the seat of House Hightower, one of the most powerful families of the Reach. The castle and lighthouse is located in the port of Oldtown atop Battle Isle, where the Honeywine widens into Whispering Sound. High Tower is a massive stepped tower with a beacon on top to guide ships into port. The color of the beacon's fire is changeable, as green flame can be used to call House Hightower's banners. The labyrinthine square fortress of unadorned black stone at the castle's foundation contains gloomy halls, vaults, and chambers. The Hightower contains a high hall. The top of the tower contains the apartments of the Lord of the Hightower. Deep vaults are located underground. The High Tower is the tallest structure in the Seven Kingdoms, even higher than the seven-hundred-foot Wall in the North.

entries.name: Kingdom of the Storm
entries.description: Kingdom of the Storm is one seven independent Kingdoms of Westeros ruled by House Durrandon, who rule all of the Stormlands. The capital of the Kingdom of the Storm is Storm's End. The first of the line was Durran Godsgrief, who according to legends built Storm's End and won the love of Elenei, the daughter of the sea god and the goddess of the wind. The Storm Kings established a powerful kingdom, and the Durrandons extended their control north to Massey's Hook and the Bay of Crabs, west into the Dornish Marches, and south to Cape Wrath.

entries.name: Stormlands
entries.description: The stormlands, is one of the constituent regions of Westeros. The Kingdom of the Storm is the sovereign nation who rules the Stormlands. The region is so-named for the savage and frequent autumn storms that batter the coast after beginning in the Summer Sea. The stormlands are ruled from the castle of Storm's End by House Durrandon. Notable bannermen of the region include Buckler, Caron, Connington, Dondarrion, Errol, Estermont, Penrose, Selmy, Staedmon, Swann, Tarth, and Wylde. Noble bastards raised in the stormlands are given the surname Storm. The stormlands are bordered to the North by the Riverlands, the west by the Reach, south by Dorne and the Sea of Dorne, and east by Shipbreaker Bay and the narrow sea. They are one of the smaller regions of Westeros, a land of harsh mountains, stony shores, and verdant forests. Major rivers include the Slayne and part of the Wendwater. The windswept plains and grasslands of the Dornish Marches, located in the south-west, serve as an effective buffer zone between the stormlands and the Reach and Dorne. There are few islands, including Tarth and Estermont. The waters around Tarth are particularly famed for their clear blue color. The stormlands are thinly populated, and their people have a reputation for being stormy like their weather. The province is known for its fierce warriors and sailors, and for moss-covered cottages among its rainy woods and green hills. Notable bannermen of the region include Buckler, Caron, Connington, Dondarrion, Errol, Estermont, Penrose, Selmy, Staedmon, Swann, Tarth, and Wylde. Noble bastards raised in the stormlands are given the surname Storm.

entries.name: House Durrandon
entries.description: House Durrandon of Storm's End was the house of the Storm Kings from the stormlands. Their seat was Storm's End, an ancient castle raised by Durran Godsgrief, the founder of their line. The Durrandon sigil was a crowned black stag on a field of gold. Their words were Ours is the Fury. Traditionally, the Storm Kings named their firstborn son and heir after the founder of their House, Durran Godsgrief. Members of the family tend to be tall and powerfully built, with black hair and blue eyes, as well as strong jawlines. They are known for their mercurial tempers.

entries.name: Realm of Dorne
entries.description: The Realm of Dorne is one seven independent which makes up the southernmost part of Westeros, ruled by Prince or Princess of House Nymeros Martell, ruling over all of Dorne. The lords of the ruling House Nymeros Martell style themselves "Prince" and "Princess" in the Rhoynish fashion. The Martells rule from their capital, Sunspear, outside of which sprawls the shadow city. Notable houses include Allyrion, Blackmont, Dayne, Fowler, Jordayne, Qorgyle, Santagar, Toland, Uller, Vaith, Wyl, and Yronwood. Dornish bastards of noble origin are given the surname Sand. Dorne is the hottest region of Westeros. The region is rocky, mountainous, arid and dry, and features the only desert on the continent. Dorne is bordered by the Sea of Dorne to the north, the Stepstones to the east, and the Summer Sea to the south. Stretched between them is the mountain range known as the Red Mountains, which separates Dorne from the stormlands to the north and the Reach to the northwest and west. There are two major passes, the Boneway and the Prince's Pass, which go through the Red Mountains to the Dornish Marches of the stormlands. Sunspear and the Water Gardens, both controlled by the ruling House Martell, are located in southeastern Dorne. Most of Dorne south of the Red Mountains is an arid wasteland. Eastern Dorne largely consists of dry, stony soil ill-suited for agriculture, while western Dorne contains deserts of red and white sand. Dorne's rivers provide some fertile lands to keep Dorne habitable. Inland water is almost as valuable as gold, and wells are jealously guarded. The trading port called Planky Town is located along the Summer Sea. Many snakes, scorpions, and sand dogs live in Dorne. Dorne is not very populated. Dornishmen differ both culturally and ethnically from other Westerosi due to the historical mass immigration of Rhoynish people and their relative isolation. Dornishmen have adopted many Rhoynish customs. Dornishmen have a reputation for hot-bloodedness and sexual licentiousness, and are still viewed with some mistrust and rivalry by Stormlands and the Reach. Dornish paint their silks instead of sewing coats of arms. Dorne contains septs for the Faith of the Seven and red temples for followers of R'hllor. Dorne provides many exotic products which are uncommon in Westeros. These products include olives, lemons, pomegranates, plums, cloth, spices, and blood oranges.
